properties.title: Longwave time transmitters — what NIC-Pip can hear
properties.note: The 40-120 kHz services a NIC-Pip board tracks (../pip/README.md). BLUE = time-code stations: they broadcast a full calendar date once a minute plus a caesium-derived carrier. AMBER = eLoran at 100 kHz: time to ~100 ns where it is receivable, but no calendar of its own, so the two classes are complementary. Circles are NOMINAL free-field reach; the real limit is the receiver's surroundings (reinforced concrete, antenna orientation) - GAIA.md siting rule 6. Note the gaps: Africa, South America, India, most of the Pacific and Indian Ocean and the whole southern hemisphere have no service in this band, so a station there runs on GNSS.
properties.sources: PTB (DCF77) · NPL (MSF) · NIST (WWVB) · VNIIFTRI (RBU) · NTSC (BPC) · NICT (JJY) · UrsaNav/DHS, ROK MOF, Chinese eLoran programme
